title: Computer Systems Design
standfirst: How a computer really works — CPU, memory, storage and the layers of abstraction above them.

description_paragraphs: This course introduces the internal organization of computers, with a focus on CPU architecture.
faculty: Prof. Ayon Chakraborty, Department of Computer Science and Engineering, IIT Madras

weeks_text.label: Week 1
weeks_text.text: Computer system overview; Representation of information; Digital logic fundamentals and basic building blocks.

weeks_text.label: Week 2
weeks_text.text: Boolean algebra foundations; SOP forms and canonical representations; Logic formulation basics.

weeks_text.label: Week 3
weeks_text.text: Logic gate transformations; POS forms; Universal gates and multilevel logic; Timing diagrams.

weeks_text.label: Week 4
weeks_text.text: Combinational circuits; Comparators; Decoders, encoders, and multiplexers.

weeks_text.label: Week 5
weeks_text.text: Adders and programmable logic arrays; Boolean simplification (K-maps); Introduction to system design.

weeks_text.label: Week 6
weeks_text.text: Practical circuit design (CircuitVerse); Display systems (7-segment displays).

weeks_text.label: Week 7
weeks_text.text: Sequential logic fundamentals; Latches and flip-flops (SR, D, JK); Clocked circuits.

weeks_text.label: Week 8
weeks_text.text: Advanced sequential circuits; Master-slave flip-flops; Circuit design using sequential elements.

weeks_text.label: Week 9
weeks_text.text: Counters (ring, Johnson, BCD); Registers and state-based circuit design.

weeks_text.label: Week 10
weeks_text.text: Processor design fundamentals; Instruction execution; Register transfer logic; Bus architecture; ISA basics.

weeks_text.label: Week 11
weeks_text.text: ALU design and computer arithmetic; Control logic design; Timing and hardware control.

weeks_text.label: Week 12
weeks_text.text: Software-based control; Processor implementation (Gajendra I); Instruction execution; Course summary.
